note: THE ONLY FILE IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT MAY NAME AN AI MODEL.
scripts/approved-model-check.mjs scans every tracked file for a string shaped like
an Anthropic model API name and fails if it finds one that is not listed here. So a
model name pasted into a function, a test, a document or a workflow turns a pull
request red, and changing which model this app sends a person's task title to is a
one-line edit to this file that a reviewer cannot miss.
THE UNDATED ALIAS IS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN ANYWHERE, including here. docs/plan.md
says the model is 'pinned by its dated API name rather than a moving alias, so the
model cannot change under the app without somebody editing a line'. Anthropic's models
page describes the alias for a model of this generation as 'a convenience pointer that
resolves to the dated ID' -- which is the moving part the plan refuses. Writing it down
would make it an approved name that some later file could use, so it is described
rather than spelled: it is the dated id below with the date removed.
EXACTLY ONE ENTRY MAY CARRY "use": true, and that is the model the function sends to.
supabase/functions/_tests/suggest_subtasks_test.ts asserts that, so a second one is a
failing test rather than an ambiguity resolved by array order.

approved.why: docs/plan.md, 'Suggest subtasks': 'Claude Haiku 4.5, pinned by its dated API name rather than a moving alias.'
approved.readAs: The 'Claude API ID' row of the model comparison table, under the Claude Haiku 4.5 column. The page's own note on that row: 'Every Claude model ID is a pinned snapshot, including the dateless IDs used from the 4.6 generation on.'
approved.retirementReadAs: The same page's 'Retirement' row for this column reads 'Not sooner than October 15, 2026'. READ THAT DATE AGAINST THE APPROVAL DATE ABOVE: it is eight days later. 'Not sooner than' is a floor rather than a date of death, and every other model in that table has a floor in September 2027. This is the owner's decision to make and it is recorded, not argued with, but it is written here so that nobody meets a dead model and goes looking for a bug: a retired model answers 404, which this function maps to the code 'refused', which looks exactly like a wrong key. Issue #185 holds it.
